cards.title: Apply for SNAP (Nutrition Assistance)
cards.summary: Arizona SNAP provides monthly food benefits via EBT. Apply through Health-e-Arizona Plus — one application covers SNAP, AHCCCS, TANF, and LIHEAP.
cards.who_qualifies: Income below 130% FPL (gross). ABAWDs 18-49 must meet 80-hour/month work requirement. Exemptions for students, caregivers, people with disabilities.
cards.how_to_apply: Apply online at healthearizonaplus.gov, call 855-432-7587, or visit local DES office.

cards.title: WIC Arizona
cards.summary: Supplemental nutrition for pregnant/postpartum women, infants, and children under 5. Provides food packages, nutrition education, and breastfeeding support.
cards.who_qualifies: Pregnant, postpartum, breastfeeding women; infants and children under 5. Income at or below 185% FPL.
cards.how_to_apply: Call Arizona WIC at 800-252-5942 or find local WIC clinic at azdhs.gov/wic.
documents_needed: Proof of pregnancy or child's age

cards.title: Phoenix Metro Food Resources
cards.summary: St. Mary's Food Bank (602-242-3663), United Food Bank (480-926-4897), Waste Not (480-941-0405), Paz de Cristo (480-464-2370). Multiple food pantries and hot meal programs across Phoenix metro.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone in need in Phoenix metro area.
cards.how_to_apply: Walk in or call. St. Mary's: 2831 N. 31st Ave, Phoenix. United Food Bank: 245 S. Nina Dr, Mesa.

cards.title: Tucson Metro Food Resources
cards.summary: Community Food Bank of Southern AZ (520-622-0525), Casa Maria (520-624-0312), Iskashitaa Refugee Network, El Rio Health food programs. Tucson area food assistance.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone in need in Tucson metro area.
cards.how_to_apply: Walk in or call. Community Food Bank: 3003 S. Country Club Rd, Tucson.

cards.title: Tribal Food Programs
cards.summary: FDPIR through ITCA (602-248-0071), Navajo Nation FDPIR (928-871-6908), GRIC Food Distribution, Salt River Pima-Maricopa, Tohono O'odham, Hopi, Pascua Yaqui food programs.
cards.who_qualifies: Tribal members and eligible households on or near reservations.
cards.how_to_apply: Contact ITCA at 602-248-0071 or specific tribal social services office.
documents_needed: Tribal enrollment or proof of AI/AN status

cards.title: AHCCCS (Arizona Medicaid)
cards.summary: Arizona's Medicaid program covers 1 in 4 Arizonans. No asset test — income-based only at 138% FPL. Covers medical, dental, behavioral health, and long-term care.
cards.who_qualifies: Income at or below 138% FPL. No asset limit. Adults, children, pregnant women, people with disabilities.
cards.how_to_apply: Apply at healthearizonaplus.gov, call 855-432-7587, or visit local DES office.

cards.title: KidsCare (CHIP)
cards.summary: Children's health insurance for families above AHCCCS income limits but below 200% FPL. Covers medical, dental, vision, behavioral health.
cards.who_qualifies: Children under 19 in families with income 138-200% FPL. Must be uninsured.
cards.how_to_apply: Apply at healthearizonaplus.gov or call 855-432-7587.

cards.title: Phoenix Metro Healthcare
cards.summary: Valleywise Health (602-344-5011) — safety-net hospital. Circle the City (602-776-3500) — homeless healthcare. Native Health (602-279-5262) — AI/AN primary care. Central Arizona Shelter Services health programs.
cards.who_qualifies: Low-income and uninsured Phoenix metro residents. Sliding scale fees.
cards.how_to_apply: Walk in or call. Valleywise: 2601 E. Roosevelt St, Phoenix.

cards.title: Indian Health Service (IHS) Arizona
cards.summary: IHS Phoenix Area (602-364-5039), IHS Tucson Area, IHS Navajo Area (928-871-5811), GRIC Health (520-562-3321), Sells IHS (520-383-7200), Whiteriver IHS, Hopi Health Center, Pascua Yaqui Health.
cards.who_qualifies: AI/AN tribal members. IHS serves all federally recognized tribal members in Arizona.
cards.how_to_apply: Contact nearest IHS facility or tribal health program. Bring tribal enrollment documentation.

cards.title: Arizona Tenant Rights
cards.summary: AZ Residential Landlord and Tenant Act (ARS §33-1301). Landlords must maintain habitable conditions. 10-business-day repair notice required. Emergency repairs (no heat/water/AC) require immediate response.
cards.who_qualifies: All Arizona renters.
cards.how_to_apply: Send written repair notice citing ARS §33-1324. Contact CLS AZ (602-258-3434) or SALA (520-623-9461) for legal help.

cards.title: Section 8 / Housing Choice Voucher
cards.summary: HAMC (Maricopa County), City of Phoenix Housing, TUCHA (Tucson). Waitlists typically closed — check portals for openings. Tribal VASH and Section 184 available for AI/AN.
cards.who_qualifies: Income below 50% AMI. Priority for elderly, disabled, families with children.
cards.how_to_apply: Contact local PHA. HAMC: 602-744-4500. City of Phoenix: 602-534-1394. TUCHA: 520-791-4619.

cards.title: Tribal Housing Programs
cards.summary: NNHA (Navajo Nation Housing Authority), GRIC Housing, SRPMIC Housing, TON Housing, HUD ONAP Phoenix, ITCA housing coordination. Section 184 Indian Home Loan Guarantee.
cards.who_qualifies: Tribal members. Section 184 available for AI/AN homebuyers nationwide.
cards.how_to_apply: Contact tribal housing authority or ITCA at 602-248-0071.

cards.title: Arizona DV Resources
cards.summary: AZ Coalition Against DV (602-279-2900) connects to 47+ local programs. Sojourner Center Phoenix (602-244-0503) — largest DV shelter in US. Emerge! Tucson (520-795-4266). DVLAP (602-258-3434) — free DV legal services statewide.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone experiencing domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault, or stalking in Arizona.
cards.how_to_apply: Call ACESDV at 602-279-2900 or National DV Hotline 800-799-7233. For legal help: DVLAP 602-258-3434.

cards.title: Tribal DV Resources
cards.summary: StrongHearts Native Helpline (844-762-8483, 24/7). ITCA VAWA programs. SALA tribal DV legal services (520-623-9461). DNA People's Legal Services for Navajo Nation DV cases.
cards.who_qualifies: Native American DV survivors. StrongHearts serves all AI/AN regardless of tribal enrollment.
cards.how_to_apply: Call StrongHearts 844-762-8483 (24/7) or SALA 520-623-9461.

cards.title: Community Legal Services AZ (CLS)
cards.summary: Free civil legal services for Phoenix metro and Maricopa/Yavapai counties — housing, benefits, DV, immigration, workers' rights, tribal members. 602-258-3434.
cards.who_qualifies: Low-income residents of Maricopa and Yavapai counties.
cards.how_to_apply: Call 602-258-3434 or visit clsaz.org.

cards.title: Southern Arizona Legal Aid (SALA)
cards.summary: Free civil legal services for 9 counties and 11 tribal reservations in Southern/SE Arizona. Housing, benefits, DV, immigration. 520-623-9461 / 800-248-6789.
cards.who_qualifies: Low-income residents of Southern Arizona and tribal members on 11 reservations.
cards.how_to_apply: Call 520-623-9461 or 800-248-6789. Visit sazlegalaid.org.

cards.title: DNA People's Legal Services
cards.summary: Primary legal aid for Navajo Nation, Hopi, and surrounding areas. Offices in Window Rock, Chinle, Tuba City, Flagstaff, and Gallup NM. 928-871-4151 / 800-789-7287.
cards.who_qualifies: Low-income tribal members in Navajo Nation, Hopi, and surrounding areas.
cards.how_to_apply: Call 928-871-4151 or 800-789-7287. Visit dnapeople.org.

cards.title: TANF / EMPOWER Program
cards.summary: Arizona TANF (EMPOWER) provides temporary cash assistance. 24-month lifetime limit — shortest in US. Maximum $278/month for family of 3. Apply through Health-e-Arizona Plus.
cards.who_qualifies: Families with children, income below TANF limits. 24-month lifetime limit applies.
cards.how_to_apply: Apply at healthearizonaplus.gov or local DES office.

cards.title: Unemployment Insurance
cards.summary: Arizona UI benefits. Maximum $240/week for 26 weeks. 15-day appeal deadline for denials — among shortest in US. File at des.az.gov.
cards.who_qualifies: Recently unemployed Arizona workers who earned sufficient wages in base period.
cards.how_to_apply: File online at des.az.gov or call 877-600-2722.

cards.title: LIHEAP & Energy Assistance
cards.summary: LIHEAP through DES (855-432-7587). APS PLUS program, APS Medical Baseline, SRP SHARE, TEP Energy Support, SW Gas assistance. Apply through Health-e-Arizona Plus.
cards.who_qualifies: Income at or below 150% FPL. Priority for elderly, disabled, families with young children.
cards.how_to_apply: Apply at healthearizonaplus.gov or local DES office. Also contact utility provider directly for company programs.

cards.title: AZ Heat Relief Network
cards.summary: Life-critical April–September. Coordinates 100+ cooling centers and water distribution sites across Arizona. Call 211 for nearest location. AZ Heat Relief: azheatrelief.org.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone in Arizona during extreme heat. No documentation required for cooling centers.
cards.how_to_apply: Call 211 or visit azheatrelief.org for nearest cooling center.

cards.title: Inter Tribal Council of Arizona (ITCA)
cards.summary: Represents 21 of AZ's 22 federally recognized tribes. Primary coordination body for tribal program referral when specific tribe is unknown. 602-248-0071.
cards.who_qualifies: AI/AN tribal members in Arizona. ITCA coordinates referrals across 21 tribes.
cards.how_to_apply: Call 602-248-0071 or visit itcaonline.com.

cards.title: Navajo Nation Services
cards.summary: Navajo Nation Social Services (928-871-6800), FDPIR (928-871-6908), Housing Authority (928-871-6462), Health (IHS Navajo Area 928-871-5811). Largest reservation in US spanning AZ/NM/UT.
cards.who_qualifies: Navajo Nation enrolled members and eligible residents.
cards.how_to_apply: Contact Navajo Nation Division of Social Services at 928-871-6800.

cards.title: AZ Center for Disability Law
cards.summary: Free legal services for Arizonans with disabilities — AHCCCS access, SSI/SSDI, abuse, discrimination. Phoenix and Tucson offices. 602-274-6287.
cards.who_qualifies: Arizonans with disabilities, including tribal members.
cards.how_to_apply: Call 602-274-6287 or visit azdisabilitylaw.org.

cards.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
cards.summary: Call or text 988 for immediate mental health crisis support. Free, confidential, 24/7. Trained counselors can help with suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, substance use, and mental health crises. Also available via chat at 988lifeline.org.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone experiencing a mental health crisis, suicidal thoughts, or emotional distress.
cards.how_to_access: Call or text 988. Chat at 988lifeline.org. For veterans, press 1 after dialing 988.

cards.title: NAMI Helpline & Support Groups
cards.summary: National Alliance on Mental Illness provides free peer support, education, and advocacy. NAMI HelpLine: 1-800-950-NAMI (6264). Family-to-Family program helps families understand mental health conditions and navigate the system.
cards.who_qualifies: Individuals with mental health conditions and their family members.
cards.how_to_access: Call 1-800-950-NAMI or text 'HELPLINE' to 62640. Find local NAMI affiliate at nami.org/find-support.

cards.title: Protection & Advocacy Organization
cards.summary: Every state has a federally mandated Protection & Advocacy (P&A) organization with legal authority to investigate abuse and neglect in psychiatric facilities. P&A organizations can enter any facility, access records, and file lawsuits. This is often the most powerful tool available for people harmed in the mental health system.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone with a disability who has experienced abuse, neglect, or rights violations in a facility.
cards.how_to_access: Find your state P&A at ndrn.org/about/ndrn-member-agencies/ or call the NDRN at 202-408-9514.

cards.title: Know Your Rights: Arizona Emergency Admission
cards.summary: If you are placed on an involuntary hold in AZ, you have rights: the initial hold cannot exceed 72 hours without a court hearing. You have the right to an attorney at the hearing. You have the right to present evidence and call witnesses. You have the right to an independent psychiatric evaluation. You can challenge the hold at any time.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone placed on an involuntary psychiatric hold or facing commitment proceedings.
cards.how_to_access: Request to speak with the patient advocate. Ask for a copy of your patient rights. Contact your state's Protection & Advocacy organization.

cards.title: Your Right to Your Psychiatric Records
cards.summary: Under HIPAA (45 CFR § 164.524), you have the right to access your complete medical record, including psychiatric treatment records. The facility must respond within 30 days. If they deny access, you can file a complaint with HHS Office for Civil Rights. Under HIPAA § 164.526, you also have the right to request amendments to inaccurate records.
cards.who_qualifies: Any current or former psychiatric patient.
cards.how_to_access: Submit a written request to the facility's Health Information Management department. If denied, file complaint at hhs.gov/ocr.

cards.title: SAMHSA National Helpline
cards.summary: Free, confidential, 24/7 treatment referral and information service for mental health and substance use disorders. Available in English and Spanish. Provides referrals to local treatment facilities, support groups, and community-based organizations.
cards.who_qualifies: Anyone seeking mental health or substance use treatment information and referrals.
